description: The line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) across eight different target labels — “cf”, “bb”, “WNBA”, “ESPN”, “NHL”, “FIFA”, “Estadio”, and a final unlabeled category — under a clean-label poisoning attack with a 10% poison rate (2.5% of total data), as evaluated on the AGNews dataset. The x-axis lists these categorical labels in order, while the y-axis represents ASR on a linear scale from 0.5 to 0.95, with tick marks at 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9. Three distinct strategies are compared: “start” (green line with circle markers), “random” (orange line with cross markers), and “end” (purple line with filled circle markers). The “start” strategy begins at ASR ≈ 0.77 for “cf”, drops sharply to ≈ 0.49 at “bb”, then rises to ≈ 0.90 at “WNBA”, fluctuates around 0.82–0.92 through “ESPN” to “Estadio”, and ends near 0.93. The “random” strategy starts at ≈ 0.66, dips to ≈ 0.51 at “bb”, peaks at ≈ 0.88 at “WNBA”, then generally increases to ≈ 0.93 at “Estadio” before falling to ≈ 0.87. The “end” strategy begins at ≈ 0.76, drops to ≈ 0.57 at “bb”, rises to ≈ 0.88 at “WNBA”, fluctuates between 0.75 and 0.90 through “ESPN” to “FIFA”, peaks at ≈ 0.96 at “Estadio”, and ends at ≈ 0.83. All three lines show significant variation across targets, with no single strategy consistently outperforming the others across all categories.
